title: What faith justifies: bare assent can exist without obedience
source_text: II. Ante omnia vero scire oportet quae sit illa fides quae justificare dicitur. Ad cujus rei intelligentiam, notandum est in Scriptura sacra quandoque dici credere, & fidem habere, illos ipsos qui Verbo Dei qualemcunque assensum praebent, & de veritate doctrinae coelestis convicti & persuasi sunt; etiamsi praeceptis ejus non obtemperent, nec vitam suam ei studeant conformare. Sic apud Joannem cap. 12. v. 42. multi ex prioribus Judaeorum dicuntur in Christum credidisse, qui tamen Christum non confitebantur, propter metum Judaeorum, & quia, ut notat Joannes, gloriam hominum magis quam gloriam Dei diligebant. Et ita quoque Simon Magus, praedicante Philippo, credidisse narratur, & ad signa & virtutes magnas quae ab eodem Philippo edebantur, obstupuisse, Act. 8. v. 13. Et tamen hoc ipso tempore, Cor ejus, arguente Petro, non erat rectum in conspectu Dei, & ipse in felle amaritudinis & iniquitatis nexu positus erat, ut videre est ejusdem capitis commate 21. & 23.
pass_a_gloss: Above all one must know what that faith is which is said to justify. For understanding this, note that sacred Scripture sometimes says that those believe and have faith who give any assent whatever to God's Word and are convinced and persuaded of the truth of heavenly doctrine, even if they do not obey its precepts nor strive to conform their life to it. So in John 12:42 many of the Jewish leaders are said to have believed in Christ, yet did not confess him for fear of the Jews, and because, as John notes, they loved the glory of men more than the glory of God. Likewise Simon Magus, when Philip preached, is narrated to have believed and to have been amazed at the great signs and wonders Philip worked (Acts 8:13); yet at that very time, when Peter rebuked him, his heart was not right before God, and he was in the gall of bitterness and the bond of iniquity (Acts 8:21, 23).
pass_b_english: Scripture sometimes calls 'faith' bare assent without obedience.
John 12:42 leaders and Simon Magus believed yet stayed unconfessing or corrupt.

choices.why: Can name mere assent in some texts.
